title: Classical Quarter-Wave Cold Mirror Stack
scientific_hypothesis: A quarter-wave Bragg stack centered at the UV reflection band edge will achieve high UV reflection while maintaining adequate SWIR transmission, with performance saturating beyond a critical pair count.
design_principle: Quarter-wave stacks produce maximum reflectance at the design wavelength when optical thickness equals λ/4; placing the Bragg condition at ~450 nm creates a high-reflection band in 300-450 nm while allowing transmission at longer wavelengths where the stack becomes transparent.
proposed_topology: Air | (hfo2 | sio2)_8 | sio2 substrate | 16 layers total
manufacturing_considerations: total layer count 16 is well below 30-layer limit
quarter-wave thicknesses are straightforward to deposit
HfO2/SiO2 pair has established deposition processes
theory_basis: Quarter-wave Bragg reflector theory for band separation
Cold mirror design principles for IR transmission with visible/UV reflection
known_risks: Quarter-wave design may not optimize both bands simultaneously
May require more pairs to achieve target UV reflection
execution_request_english: Design a periodic multilayer stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack structure: Air | (hfo2 | SiO2 (Lemarchand))_8 | SiO2 (Lemarchand) substrate, totaling 16 layers. Optimize the quarter-wave reference wavelength and a uniform thickness scale factor to maximize transmission in 1000-1700 nm band and reflection in 300-450 nm band. Use only hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) materials. Evaluate performance at normal incidence, unpolarized light.
